summary.intent: Evaluate how well the wisp-plugins set worked for front-end work and design ideation across the orin-dx and pages/techworx projects, then act on the findings: remove process ceremony from the plugins, and tighten both the ADRs and the way they are written.
summary.outcome: Four investigations found the plugins are spec-first and converge-only, with no visual or exploratory mode. The ceremony removals were then applied and pushed to trail #386: estimator, TBD ban, per-task commits, single-source versions, and all 44 persona backstories after an ablation showed no measurable effect. ADRs 011-017 were condensed, and the ADR guidance was reworded around reader outcome with a warn-only style check.

repo: The 10 wisp-plugins form a spec-driven lifecycle (weaver, vanguard, scribe/muse, navigator, smith, courier, with sentinel and ranger as verifiers) using typed JSON handoffs in shared/schemas and default-fail gates.

No plugin has any browser, screenshot, Storybook, Playwright or visual capability. spec@1 has no fields for tokens, layout, breakpoints or copy, so a spec can pass the muse gate while saying nothing about appearance.
Muse docs reference a ranger accessibility taxonomy that was never implemented, so implemented a11y is never checked.

Across ~810 session files, plugin agents were used in only two real sessions (orin-dx b8d16e96 and pages 24655582). Most files are subagent transcripts, and ideation ran through Artifacts, forks, general-purpose agents and local dev servers instead.

The gate caught real cross-spec contradictions and contrast and behavioural defects, but late blockers were mostly wording churn. Visual defects (NavSheet not full screen, wrong breakpoints, NaN% on the brand page) were found by the user's eye or later audits.
The orchestrator ignored the gate's 3-retry escalation rule and carried on with an 'owner-directed gate pass' without asking the user.
The reasoning field is ~12% of handback characters but under 0.1% of subagent token spend, so it was kept.

Backstory ablation (3 agents, 5 runs per condition, seeded defects): 5/5 defects found with and without, same size and cost. This is evidence of no measurable effect, not proof, since the defects were easy.
Generated Codex output in dist/ must be regenerated with `just marketplace-sync` after editing shared references, otherwise `just check` fails.

ADR guidance lives in shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md, and scripts/check-adr-style.py is a warn-only check (450-word threshold plus transient-marker patterns) that runs in `just check`.
orin-dx-site is not a git repo and holds only brand/ artifacts. All specs, plans, reviews and audits live in ~/projects/pages/docs.

code.finding: The cognitive tier model has no divergent or ideation mode, so the architecture only converges.
Smith accepts a spec with no plan, but still runs recon, mutator, reviewer and a binding exit-gate. There is no spike or throwaway mode.
No fields for visual intent (tokens, layout, breakpoints, motion, copy).
The single-source version check had to keep failing when a plugin is missing from a marketplace or a root entry lacks a version (Entire finding, fixed in 133d1537).
Now pins a four-part agent structure (constitution, optional load_first, goal, judgment, output) and asserts backstory is never opened.

workflow: Check the corpus before analysing: the directory file counts were mostly subagent transcripts, which corrected the earlier session-count claim.
Run a mechanical scan first (skill and agent invocation counts) before delegating qualitative analysis to parallel subagents.
Validate scorer logic before trusting results. The first ablation scorer matched the fixtures trivially and had to be rescored on agent output only.
Measure before removing ceremony: the reasoning field was kept after measurement, the backstories removed after an ablation.

Agents writing ADRs tend to narrate the session with run counts and dates. Evidence belongs in an evaluation log, and ADRs should keep decision, why, rejected alternatives, consequences with a revisit trigger, and an evidence pointer.
The user prefers goal and outcome guidance over prescriptive targets, and scannable consistent structure (bullets, fixed headings) for human readers.
Subagent reports are unverified input. Cross-check them and do not treat them as user approval.

friction: A transient GitHub storage error failed the first push twice and needed a retry.
The first ablation smoke run reported 0 turns for the without-backstory condition, apparently because the subagent ran in the background. The prompts were changed to force foreground runs.
The first full ablation run failed because the PR 483 diff had vanished from the temp directory and had to be re-fetched.
The ADR word-count target was initially set at 350, which flagged nearly every record, so it was raised to 450. The user then said targets are too prescriptive.
The condensed ADRs landed at 417-519 words, above the 250-350 target, because cutting further would have lost rejected alternatives or guardrails.
A test padded too little to cross the 350-word threshold, so the test was fixed, not the check.
`just check` failed once because generated Codex output was stale after a reference edit, and needed a marketplace-sync.
The user had to repeatedly ask for visual examples ('show me') because specs and text descriptions could not be judged without renders.
open_items: Trail #386 needs approval, and the three Entire findings on change 4 are replied to but not resolved.
orin-dx PRs are waiting for Entire to open them because the pr-bot token cannot be minted on this machine.
Old Monokl changesets with breaking notes inside bullets were not rewritten, so they won't appear in 'Read before merging'.
Whether the ceremony removals reduce gate rounds, turns or tokens is unmeasured. docs/evaluation-runbook.md is ready for this after release.
ADR 016 (about 500 words) and older ADRs 007-009 are still flagged by the style check and could be trimmed.
User decisions pending: Caliper's hard-coded rustup path, Pages' `rtk` rule, and orin-dx-site's status.

The proposed front-end gaps remain unbuilt: a sketch/spike mode, a visual exploration agent, a browser/screenshot capability kind, a prototype-to-spec promote path, visual criteria in specs, and cross-session decision memory.
The ablation covered only three agents on easy defects. Harder-defect or other-agent runs could change the backstory conclusion, and ADR 017 says how to restore one.
The final guidance rewrite (goal-oriented ADR guidance) was being committed and pushed when the transcript ended, so its push status is unconfirmed.
